scenes.title: Data Transfer & Egress Costs
scenes.narration: Moving data in the cloud is often cheap or free coming in, but data leaving a region or provider can incur significant egress charges that surprise teams.

scenes.title: How Transfer Is Priced
bullets: Data ingress into the cloud is usually free, which lulls teams into ignoring transfer costs.
Egress out to the internet or another region is billed per gigabyte and adds up fast.
Traffic within the same availability zone is typically the cheapest path.
scenes.narration: Cloud networking pricing follows a consistent pattern. Bringing data in is generally free, so teams rarely think about it. Sending data out to the internet or across regions is charged per gigabyte and can dominate a bill at scale. Keeping traffic within a single availability zone is usually the least expensive option.

scenes.title: Cost by Path
steps: Across zones in a region: modest
scenes.narration: Transfer cost rises with distance and boundaries crossed. Traffic inside one availability zone is the cheapest. Crossing zones within a region adds a modest charge, crossing regions costs more, and sending data out to the public internet is the most expensive of all. Designing data flows with this hierarchy in mind saves real money.

scenes.title: Reducing Egress
scenes.narration: Egress bills usually come from a few habits: chatty cross-region traffic, serving large files straight from storage to the internet, and repeatedly copying the same data. The remedies are to co-locate compute next to data, front public delivery with a CDN, and compress and cache to move fewer bytes. Small design changes here yield large savings.

scenes.title: Keeping Traffic Private with VPC Endpoints
scenes.code:
# Create a gateway endpoint so S3 traffic stays on the AWS network
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
  --vpc-id vpc-0abcd1234 \
  --service-name com.amazonaws.us-east-1.s3 \
  --route-table-ids rtb-0abcd1234
scenes.narration: A VPC endpoint keeps traffic to services like S3 on the provider's private network instead of routing it over the internet. This command creates a gateway endpoint for S3 in your VPC. Beyond improving security, it avoids NAT gateway data processing charges, which is a common hidden source of transfer cost.

scenes.text: Ingress is cheap but egress is not — co-locate compute with data, avoid needless cross-region and internet transfer, and use endpoints to keep traffic private.
scenes.narration: Data coming in is nearly free while data going out is not. Co-locating compute with data, minimizing cross-region and internet transfer, and using private endpoints keep egress from quietly draining your budget.
